subject: FinWise load test coordination — performance & SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@finwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinWise: post-demo SLOs and load test plan

Thanks again for the demo call today, Ellen — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test on the calendar.

Summary from our discussion:
- Target SLOs: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for standard short responses (non-streaming). For streaming use cases, we agreed to measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target of <= 150ms and steady-state chunk latency < 100ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: target sustained throughput ~120 req/s with bursts to 400 req/s, expected concurrency up to ~60 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: you require chunked streaming support and the ability to push partial responses to the client.
- Success criteria: no more than 2% >95th violations during the window and no reliability errors (5xx) lasting > 30s.

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood provides a test account (scoped API token), allowlist IP ranges, and a k6/Locust script baseline for your engineering team. See attached initial k6 script (finwise_k6_script_v1.js).
2) Customer runs a scheduled load test window. Proposed window: Sun Mar 22, 2026 10:00–12:00 PT (we can adjust). Please confirm.
3) Redwood standby: Aditya will monitor runtime telemetry and provide a runbook/triage channel.

Attachments: finwise_k6_script_v1.js (baseline), redwood-test-account-details.md (test creds and scopes).

If the window works, we’ll send the allowlist IPs and scoped token by end of day. Happy to jump on a short sync beforehand if you want a canary test.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Ellen Park <ellen@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinWise: post-demo SLOs and load test plan

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick items from our side: \

- The FinWise performance team would prefer the 95th percentile target for the standard flows to be <= 250ms if possible. Can your team confirm whether that’s realistic for our payload sizes (typically 200–800 tokens)?
- We absolutely need streaming TTFB around 100–150ms and per-chunk latency as you noted.
- Confirming the proposed window (Sun Mar 22, 10:00–12:00 PT) works for our engineers.

Two asks before we start:
1) Please send the allowlist IP ranges and the scoped test token (or instructions for a token with limited scope). Our security team will use those to validate access.
2) Can you provide a short doc with the expected metrics/labels the Redwood telemetry will publish (latency percentiles, concurrency, token usage, model variant)? Our SREs want to match metrics on their side.

Happy to include Jake Turner (our performance lead) if needed — he’ll be helping run the k6 job.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Infrastructure
FinWise
ellen@finwise.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinWise: post-demo SLOs and load test plan

Looping in a quick engineering note:
- 250ms 95th for 200–800 token responses is aggressive but potentially achievable with the right model sizing and quantization profile. We should baseline with the customer payload and a 2x replica pool for the test.
- For the streaming TTFB ~100–150ms we’ll need to ensure the model variant supports streaming-friendly kernels and that batching is tuned for low latency (small batch tail).

Action items for infra: I’ll prepare a scoped test account and k6 example with ramp and canary phases. Attached are internal k6 setup notes (k6-setup-notes.md). I’ll also provide the exact allowlist IP ranges and a test token TTL.

Aditya
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya@redwood.com

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinWise: post-demo SLOs and load test plan

If that all looks good we’ll be on standby Sunday at 09:30 PT to run a short canary and then the 10:00 window.

From: Ellen Park <ellen@finwise.com>

Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finwise.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinWise: post-demo SLOs and load test plan

Thanks — that looks good. We confirmed internally: Jake will run the k6 job and our SREs will compare metrics against the runbook mapping. Token reception via the secure channel succeeded.

Two quick requests for the canary:
- Can we run a 10-minute canary at 09:40 PT with 5–10 concurrent sessions and one short-streaming flow to validate TTFB?
- Please post the Redwood runbook link and the allowlist IP blocks to our shared Slack channel #finwise-redwood so our infra team can pull them quickly.

We’ll proceed with the 10:00–12:00 PT window after the canary. Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jake will send results and any observed spikes to this thread and to your runbook issue tracker.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Infrastructure
FinWise
ellen@finwise.com
